RelayLaunch helps local service businesses get found in AI-assisted search, get booked, and keep the customers they already have, in that order. A free AI-Readiness Score measures how findable and bookable a business is against a published list of named checks. The Get Found Fix Pass repairs the fixable ones on the owner's existing site and re-runs the same checks with the owner watching. Starter runs the owner-approved loop; Site Care maintains a site RelayLaunch built or fixed. Every action is[truncated] · OODA Loop methodology. Observe-Orient-Decide-Act cycle for strategic decisions. Agents run parallel OODA loops, surface conflicting orientations, and converge on actionable strategy through structured debate. · Design Thinking methodology. Empathize-Define-Ideate-Prototype-Test cycle for creative problem-solving. Agents explore the problem space before converging on solutions. · Monte Carlo methodology. Probabilistic risk assessment using scenario modeling. Agents assign probability distributions to outcomes and identify tail risks that deterministic analysis misses. · M&A Framework methodology. Full evaluation framework for major decisions: partnerships, acquisitions, large investments. Structured like institutional due diligence with financial, operational, and strategic lenses. · Kantian + Utilitarian methodology. Dual-framework ethical analysis. Agents apply both deontological (duty-based) and consequentialist (outcome-based) reasoning, then surface where the frameworks disagree. · AARRR Pirate Metrics methodology. Acquisition-Activation-Retention-Revenue-Referral framework for growth strategy. Each agent owns one metric and argues for prioritization. · Architecture Decision Records methodology. Structured technical decision-making using ADR methodology. Agents evaluate context, options, and consequences to produce a defensible architecture decision. · Porter's Five Forces methodology. Competitive landscape analysis using Porter's framework. Agents assess competitive rivalry, supplier power, buyer power, threat of substitution, and threat of new entry. · Incident Command methodology. Incident Command System adapted for business crises. Structured rapid response with clear roles, communication protocols, and escalation paths. · DCF + Comparables methodology. Investment decision framework combining discounted cash flow analysis with comparable transaction benchmarks. Quantitative rigor meets qualitative judgment. · Six Sigma methodology. Six Sigma DMAIC process for quality improvement decisions. Define-Measure-Analyze-Improve-Control applied to business processes and product quality. · Scientific Method methodology. Hypothesis-driven decision-making using scientific method. Agents form hypotheses, design experiments, predict outcomes, and evaluate evidence. · Game Theory methodology. Game-theoretic competitive strategy. Agents model competitor moves, identify Nash equilibria, and recommend dominant strategies accounting for multi-player dynamics. · Regulatory Impact Assessment methodology. Policy and regulatory decision analysis. Evaluates compliance requirements, regulatory risk, and the cost-benefit of policy options across multiple jurisdictions. · Network Optimization methodology. Supply chain resilience and optimization analysis. Agents map dependencies, identify single points of failure, model disruption scenarios, and recommend diversification strategies. · Organizational Design methodology. People strategy and organizational design analysis. Agents evaluate team structure, culture dynamics, talent acquisition, retention levers, and succession planning. · Impact Assessment methodology. Environmental, Social, and Governance analysis for strategic decisions. Agents evaluate climate risk, social impact, governance quality, and alignment with reporting frameworks. · Turn a completed council review into a written summary: the recommendation, the dissent, the points that did not reach agreement, and the sources each claim rests on. Internal review output, not a certified or audited rep[truncated]

Production-grade, real-time threat detection for Python LLM and agentic applications. Guardian SDK protects the full agentic loop — input to the model, output from the model, every tool call an agent makes, every value tools return into the agent's context, and the compiled/parallel execution plans agent runtimes dispatch — across text, images, audio, and video. 170+ threat categories, 1,700+ regex patterns, 3,400+ semantic fingerprints on the API tier. Also available fully self-hosted (pip i[truncated] · Scan an incoming prompt or agentic input before it reaches the model. Runs multiple sequential detection layers: regex pattern matching with obfuscation normalization, ONNX MiniLM-L6-v2 semantic analysis, behavioral session heuristics, ML gradient-boosted inference, and visual/cross-modal analysis for image inputs. Returns ALLOW, CHALLENGE, or BLOCK with threat level, threat types, confidence, and reasoning. Covers 170+ threat categories on the API tier. · Scan an LLM response before it reaches the user or downstream agents. Detects jailbreak compliance, constraint removal acknowledgments, system prompt revelation, role abandonment, credential/PHI leakage, and other signals that indicate the model was successfully manipulated. Returns suppressed (bool) and a safe replacement response when suppression is triggered. AdversarialLearner simultaneously updates the threat database for improved pre-flight detection. · Validate a tool call and its arguments before the agent executes it. Detects shell injection, path traversal, data exfiltration infrastructure, destructive operations (rm -rf, DROP TABLE), credential theft attempts, package installs from untrusted sources, and malicious flag combinations. Returns is_dangerous (bool), risk_score, and threat_categories. The same gate scales to compiled/parallel execution plans (DAGs): the AgenticExecutionMonitor decomposes a plan, validates each node, and flags dan[truncated] · Scan a tool return value before it re-enters the agent's context window. Detects indirect prompt injection payloads embedded in web pages, documents, API responses, database records, and any external content the agent retrieves. Returns is_injection (bool), injection_score, and matched patterns. · Validate a compiled/parallel agent execution plan (DAG) before the runtime dispatches it. Decomposes the plan, validates each node through the tool-call gate, and flags dangerous calls hidden in 'atomic'/parallel no-inspect batches, guard-disable steps ordered before payloads, hidden nodes absent from the approval summary, dependency cycles, and agent-swarm fan-out escalation across a session. Returns ALLOW/CHALLENGE/BLOCK with risk_score, node_count, dangerous_node_ids, and signals. · ScopeGuard (a separate, paid-only product on the Ethicore Engine platform): decide whether a user turn is in-purpose for a narrow bot, given the deployer's declared scope (allow_domains + deny_task_types).
